title: Superbot bridges induce neuronal gap closure in scratched monolayers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Superbot bridges induce neuronal gap closure in scratched monolayers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Fused Anthrobot assemblies (superbots) placed across a scratch in a human neuronal monolayer induce substantial regrowth of neuronal tissue beneath them within 72 hours, forming a stitch that connects the two sides of the scratch.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Strikingly, within the next 72 h upon inoculation of the superbot into the tissue scratch on day 0, we observed a substantial regrowth of the native tissue taking place (i.e., gap closure), resulting in the formation of a stitch right underneath the “superbot bridge,” connecting the two sides of the scratch (Figure 6B).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues”. Scope: Superbots of fused NHBE-derived Anthrobots on scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers in vitro

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap closure, location, and timing are objectively image-measurable. Public images support the reported phenomenon, but small selected samples and control limitations weaken the induction claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify neuron-positive area connecting both scratch sides over 72 hours beneath superbots versus matched scratch-only, agarose, and placement controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Scratch-only temporal controls and complete raw image series may be limited.

Only five of ten bridges maintained connectivity for analysis.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.84
operationalizability: 0.96
discriminating power: 0.65
data existence: 0.66
data adequacy: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Local neuronal coverage at 72 hours under a superbot versus elsewhere on the scratch is a clear endpoint. The paper shows examples and states a qualitative regrowth result, with the images and measurements available on request. Example panels are not the replicate set, so the induction claim still needs the withheld images or a new scratch series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Place fused Anthrobot bridges across scratches in human neuronal monolayers and measure neuronal coverage under the bridge at 72 hours versus the same scratch without a bridge. Closure confined to the bridge, forming a stitch between the two sides, would support induction; no local regrowth, or regrowth everywhere along the scratch, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The neuronal cultures are one hiNSC differentiation protocol.

Replicate images and coverage values are not deposited; the paper reports that five of ten bridges stayed in place.

A stitch under the bot can be passive edge apposition rather than induced regrowth.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.18
data existence: 0.2
